text.formula: The beads only bob up and down…
…a shorter wave is a higher note…
…and tied at both ends, only whole waves fit

youtube.title: What is a wave? Explained in 30 seconds 🌊 #shorts
youtube.description:
Step 1: in a wave nothing travels but the shape; each bead only moves up and down. Step 2: speed = frequency × wavelength, so a shorter wave is a higher note. Step 3: a string tied at both ends only fits whole half-waves: the harmonics.

text.formula: …close one end: only the odd ones

youtube.title: The harmonic series: why a flute and a clarinet differ 🎶 #shorts
youtube.description:
A string and an open tube can sing every harmonic: 1, 2, 3, 4 … A tube closed at one end can only sing the odd ones: 1, 3, 5 … The dust in the tubes shows where the air stands still.

#satisfying #simulation #shorts

text.formula: Circles add up to a square…

youtube.title: Fourier series: circles that draw any wave 🔵 #shorts
youtube.description:
Each spinning circle is one sine wave. Stack them, biggest first, and they draw a square wave, a sawtooth, a triangle. Sound works the same way: every note is a sum of sines.

hook.text: What happens when two waves meet?

youtube.title: When two waves meet: beats and interference 〰️ #shorts
youtube.description:
Waves simply add. In time, two close notes drift in and out of step and you hear beats. In space, two sources make lines where crest meets trough and the water stays still.

hook.text: Why do some notes sound good together?

youtube.title: Why some notes sound good together 🎹 #shorts
youtube.description:
Two notes sound sweet when their frequencies make a simple ratio: 2:1 (octave), 3:2 (fifth), 4:3 (fourth). An oscilloscope shows it: simple ratios draw calm closed shapes, messy ones scribble.

hook.text: Why does a siren change its pitch?

youtube.title: The Doppler effect and the sonic boom 🚑 #shorts
youtube.description:
A moving source squeezes the waves ahead (higher pitch) and stretches them behind (lower pitch). Faster than its own sound, the waves pile up into a cone: the sonic boom.

#satisfying #simulation #shorts

youtube.title: From a magnet to a wire to a coil 🧲⚡ #shorts
youtube.description:
Iron filings show the field of a bar magnet, of a single wire carrying a current (circles), and of a coil, which looks just like the bar magnet. That is how electromagnets and motors work.

hook.text: What do numbers look like on a circle?

youtube.title: Three secrets of numbers on a circle 🌻 #shorts
youtube.description:
Multiply around a circle and a heart shape appears. Jump by a fraction and you close into a star. Jump by the golden angle and you never land twice: that is how sunflowers pack their seeds.
